availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #377. The API states no publication time and keeps no vintages (it serves the current table), so the instant is Treasury's published schedule, not a measured one, and it is NOT VERIFIED from this environment: fiscaldata.treasury.gov (the dataset page that states the schedule) is refused by the proxy, and only the api. host is reachable. The schedule used is that the Daily Treasury Statement for a business day is published at 4:00 PM ET on the next business day. 16:30 ET is declared, 30 minutes after it and the same margin the bill-rate declaration takes over its bulk file's time, so a decision at 16:00 ET on that next business day does not read it and the first decision that does is the one after. The series' meaning and units were checked against FRED's WTREGEN (the H.4.1's weekly average of the TGA): the 7-calendar-day average of the daily closing balances ending each Wednesday, carried across weekends and holidays, matches WTREGEN to within 0.0009 USD billions on every one of the 451 Wednesdays 2018-01-17 to 2026-09-02 (tests/fixtures/snapshots/dts_inputs against funding_inputs/fred-macro-latest-vintage), which also settles that the line named 'Federal Reserve Account', 'Treasury General Account (TGA)' and 'Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance' are one series across the renames. Units: the statement reports USD millions; the adapter divides by 1000.
availability_provenance.publication: Daily Treasury Statement (Bureau of the Fiscal Service), Table I, Operating Cash Balance, served as Fiscal Data's accounting/dts/operating_cash_balance table; published at 4:00 PM ET on the business day after the date it describes.

coverage: Treasury General Account closing balance, daily, 2018-01-02 onwards in the tracked snapshots (the table runs from 2005-10-03)

The closing-balance line has had three names (the Federal Reserve Account, the Treasury General Account (TGA), and from the April 2022 redesign the Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance, whose value sits in the open_today_bal column); the adapter reads each in its own column and refuses a date with two closing balances. Each snapshot is one unmodified, year-wide response; a re-fetch can differ.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445, from the tracked snapshots of the Desk's operation results (tests/fixtures/snapshots/on_rrp_inputs/nyfed_on_rrp, the same records nyfed_on_rrp reads). The Desk states no publication clock time (nyfed_on_rrp.availability_provenance). The evidence is each record's lastUpdated, the time the Desk last wrote it: a record whose lastUpdated is on its own operation date is public no later than that time, because it cannot be written later than it was first written. Over the 1997 operation dates 2018-01-02 to 2025-12-31 that carry a reverse-repo operation, 1985 have every record last written on the operation date at or before 15:00 New York time (earliest 13:15:20, median 13:15:52, 99th percentile 13:22:17, latest 14:43:00 on 2023-07-17, an operation delayed to close at 14:00). The other 12 are not provable and are excluded, so the column is empty on them: 10 were written again on a later date (2018-03-29, 2018-12-04, 2019-04-18, 2020-04-09, 2020-07-02, 2021-04-01, 2021-09-03, 2021-09-10, 2022-11-17, 2023-01-05), where lastUpdated says nothing about the first write, and 2 were last written on their own date after 15:00 (2018-02-16 at 16:43:22, a record annotated that $14.050 billion less settled than was accepted, and the 2024-10-16 small-value exercise at 16:50:30) and are excluded because the time of their first write is not known. The reading assumes the Desk's API serves a record from the time it is written, which is not stated anywhere and cannot be verified from outside; a record could be written to the Desk's database before the API shows it. 15:00 is declared, 17 minutes after the latest included lastUpdated and an hour before the 16:00 decision. Note the exclusion looks at a record's later rewrites, which no forecast at the time could know; it only removes days, and whether a record was rewritten years later is unrelated to the spread.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed reverse repo operation results: the operation closes at 13:15 ET and the Desk's API carries the summary of results, last written at lastUpdated; 15:00 ET on the operation date is the declared availability instant for a day whose records were all last written on that date at or before 15:00.

coverage: overnight reverse repo amounts accepted on the operation date, for the dates whose evidence is proven

Treasury's Daily Treasury Bill Rates page (tests/fixtures/snapshots/treasury_bill_rates_page, fetched 2026-10-09T03:02:41Z, sha256 949a9940...) states that the par yields are derived from indicative bid-side quotations 'obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York at or near 3:30 PM each trading day' and states no time at which the rates are posted. The tracked yearly exports carry a retrieval time only (one fetch, 2026-09-14, or the commit time of the file) and the page keeps no vintages, so no archived copy dates a first posting; the page fetched here already carried the 8 October row when read, some 8 hours after the close. The Federal Reserve's H.15 file, which republishes the rates, is at 16:30 ET (treasury_bill_rates.availability_provenance). Quotes are struck at about 15:30, so a posting before 16:00 would leave under 30 minutes and nothing shows it happened. The input is therefore declared at the end of its own day, which no decision at 16:00 on the same day reads; it enters no nowcast and no forecast of this track.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #445. spread_nowcast_bps on the row of day r is computed by repo_model.nowcast from the spread of day r - 1 (SOFR is published at about 08:00 ET on r and declared public at 15:00 ET on r, nyfed_sofr.release_lag) and earlier days, the same-day reverse repo of r (nyfed_on_rrp_sameday, 15:00 on r), the gross Treasury settlement of r (treasury_auctions.scheduled_availability, 15:00 on the panel day before r) and the calendar. Its latest input is therefore public at 15:00 ET on r. Its ridge is fitted on pairs whose target row is at most r - 1. tests/test_nowcast.py checks both by changing every input from row r on, and every label from row r on, and asking the nowcast to stay the same.

The constituents' timing is declared here, not through contract.FEATURE_FIELDS, because the as-of rule reads a derived feature at the latest row where every constituent is observable, which would put SOFR's lag on a value that is built for a day before SOFR is public.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 8 October 2026 for #425. The same operation-results endpoint as nyfed_srf and nyfed_on_rrp (markets.newyorkfed.org/api/rp/results/search.json), saved here a calendar year at a time for 2018-01-01 to 2025-12-31 and read for every repo operation, not only the facility's overnight ones. The Desk states no clock time at which results are published; the one timestamp in each record is lastUpdated, a write time. The adapter records it per operation date (the latest lastUpdated of the date's kept operations, New York time) and reads a date's values at the later of that and the declaration below, so a rewritten record can only make a value later. On the snapshots, lastUpdated is on the operation date for all but 2023-05-11 (09:29 the next day, before the declaration), and is later than the declaration for two dates, 2021-09-03 and 2021-09-10, both rewritten on 2021-09-16. The declaration is #45's and #127's conservative reading for the same endpoint: 16:00 ET on the next business day. Extended on 14 October 2026 for #766: one more snapshot, 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-03 (a partial year, fetched on 2026-10-14), beside the eight yearly ones, which are unchanged; coverage_end is 2026-09-03. Ingestion only: no 2026 day is scored (docs/decisions/lockbox.md) and the published panel still stops at 2025-12-31.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed repo operation results: the temporary open market operations of 2019 and 2020 and the Standing Repo Facility from 2021-07-29. Operations close between 08:30 and 13:45 ET and the Desk publishes a summary of results after each, at no stated clock time. 16:00 ET on the next business day is the conservative availability instant declared here.

coverage: Repo operations (overnight and term) amounts accepted and submitted, the amount-weighted rate accepted and the number of operations that accepted anything, per operation date, 2019-09-17 to 2026-09-03 in the tracked snapshots (the six test operations of 2018-05-09 to 2019-05-13 are left out), and the term repos outstanding per business day over the same dates

field_meanings.repo_accepted: A take-up demand signal: the amount the Desk accepted on the operation date, summed over the date's operations. It is not the amount outstanding: a term repo is counted once, on its operation date, and not on the days until it matures.
field_meanings.repo_ops_accepting: The number of the date's operations that accepted anything.
field_meanings.repo_rate: The accepted-amount-weighted mean of the securities' weighted-average rate accepted, in percent; absent on a date where nothing was accepted at a stated rate.
field_meanings.repo_submitted: The amount submitted on the operation date, summed over the date's operations: a take-up demand signal, as repo_accepted.
field_meanings.repo_term_outstanding: The cash in the system from term repos: the amount accepted on term repos with settlement on or before the business day and maturity after it (#659). Rebuilt from settlementDate and maturityDate across the snapshot files; 0.0 on a covered business day with nothing outstanding.

nyfed_repo_ops.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#425), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes. repo_accepted and repo_submitted are totalAmtAccepted and totalAmtSubmitted summed over every operation of an operationDate whose operationType is 'Repo' (overnight or term), in USD billions (the API serves US dollars). repo_rate is the accepted-amount-weighted mean of the securities' percentWeightedAverageRate, in percent, and is absent on a date where nothing was accepted at a stated rate. repo_ops_accepting counts the date's operations that accepted anything. Operations the Desk names small-value exercises in the note are left out, and so are the six operations of 64 to 66 million dollars before the facility's first day, 2019-09-17 (facility_start; 2018-05-09 to 2019-05-13): they are operational tests, not take-up, and no Fed repo was offered to the market before it (#659, data meaning decided by Nicholas Beroud on eleonorabjornberg/repo-market-liquidity#1). A date with no operation has no row. The measurement columns (fed_liquidity.assemble) read it as zero before facility_start (a structural zero) and from the Standing Repo Facility's first day, 2021-07-29, and as missing from facility_start to the day before it (2021-07-28), in the years the Desk did not operate on every day; the tracked snapshots hold no such date. A date after coverage_end, the last date the tracked snapshots cover, is refused, never read as zero. repo_accepted and repo_submitted are demand signals (field_meanings); repo_term_outstanding is the term repos outstanding, so that no different measure sits under the same name. Each yearly snapshot is one unmodified search response; the year in progress changes when re-fetched.
nyfed_repo_ops.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 9 October 2026 for #442. A sensitivity test of nyfed_repo_ops, not a replacement: the same endpoint, the same yearly snapshots (nyfed_repo_ops/), read at a less conservative instant. Operations close at 13:45 ET (and 08:30 ET from 26 June 2025). The Desk states no clock time at which results are published; the one timestamp, lastUpdated, is a write time. On the facility's 1,617 overnight operations (2021-07-29 to 2026-09-30) it falls a median 0.7 minutes after the close and 3.3 minutes at the 99th percentile (nyfed_srf.availability_provenance, #127). On the tracked snapshots (2018-05-09 to 2025-12-31) only five operation dates were written after 16:00 ET on their own date: 2021-12-28 at 16:10 and 2023-03-22 at 17:22 the same day, 2023-05-11 at 09:29 on the next day, and 2021-09-03 and 2021-09-10, both rewritten on 2021-09-16. A date is therefore read as public at 16:00 ET on its own date, and a date written later is read at the next decision instant at or after its write time (ingest.repo_operation_same_day_available_at); the two rewritten dates stay on the conservative reading because a rewrite cannot establish a first publication. The panel columns (fed_liquidity, suffix _sameday) read a withheld date as zero, as a date with no operation. The published nyfed_srf declaration (16:00 ET on the next business day) is not changed by this source; changing it is Eleonora's decision.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 11 October 2026 for #545. Not a fetched series: the columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.projected_reserves. net_settlement_ahead_{k}d is the announced net Treasury settlement of the next k business days, each auction counted from its announcemt_date as at the declared instant of treasury_auction_net_settlement (12:00 ET on the row's own day). proj_reserves_h{h}, proj_dist_h{h} and proj_change_h{h} roll the reserve level that the as-of rule reads at the row's 16:00 decision forward to the scored day through the flows public by then; every read goes through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.projected_reserves.check_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a column that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/projected_reserves.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL), tga_daily (Daily Treasury Statement), on_rrp, bank_total_assets (H.8) and treasury_auction_net_settlement, each under its own lag.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads every input
projected_reserves_columns.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#545), declared here and not in metadata/sources.json for the reason treasury_auction_net_settlement gives. Read only by a track that switches the columns on (repo_model.projected_reserves.COLUMN_FIELDS). The projection rolls the weekly reserve level forward by the Fed liability identity (Treasury account and facility gain what reserves lose); it ignores currency and the Federal Reserve's own asset changes, and it adds no separate runoff leg: the Treasury leg is inside the announced net settlement, and agency MBS paydowns are in no tracked series. No announced TGA path is tracked, so persistence applies beyond the settlements and the expected tax receipts.
projected_reserves_columns.provider: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

release_lag.note: Declared 11 October 2026 (#545). The value on the row of day t uses only reads the as-of rule allows at 16:00 ET on t (availability_provenance), so the 16:00 ET decision of t reads it.

projected_reserves_columns.reviewed_note: Derived columns: no structural zeros. A hole is a missing input or a row where the rule has no read.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 11 October 2026 for #587. Not a fetched series: the column is computed per panel row by repo_model.satiation. satiation_roll is the declared low quantile of the reserves-to-assets ratios that the as-of rule reads at each of the last 504 panel rows' own 16:00 decisions, up to and including the row's own; each leg of the ratio (reserve_balances, H.4.1; bank_total_assets, H.8) is read at its own latest public row through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.satiation.check_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a level that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/satiation_587.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL) and bank_total_assets (H.8), each under its own lag.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads both legs of the ratio

The level is a low quantile of a step series (the ratio changes only when a weekly release lands), so each week's ratio counts for as many panel rows as it is the latest public one.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #598. Not a fetched series: the columns are computed per panel row by repo_model.satiation.build_distance_columns. satiation_dist_roll is the reserves-to-assets ratio that the as-of rule reads at the row's own 16:00 decision minus satiation_roll's level at that row (the rolling level of #587, constants unchanged); satiation_hinge_roll is the percentage points by which that ratio is below the level, 0 at or above it. Each leg of the ratio (reserve_balances, H.4.1 WRESBAL; bank_total_assets, H.8) is read at its own latest public row through asof.InformationRule with the scored row one after the decision row, and repo_model.satiation.check_distance_no_future rebuilds a row from the panel cut at it and refuses a value that differs. A row's value is therefore public at 16:00 on its own date.
availability_provenance.publication: metadata/satiation_distance_598.json declares the rule; its inputs are the registry's reserve_balances (H.4.1 WRESBAL) and bank_total_assets (H.8), each under its own lag, and the rolling level of metadata/satiation_587.json.

coverage: one value per panel day to 2025-12-31, from the first day on which the as-of rule reads both legs of the ratio
satiation_distance_columns.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#598), declared here and not in metadata/sources.json for the reason satiation_columns gives. Read only by a track that switches the columns on (repo_model.satiation.DISTANCE_COLUMN_FIELDS). The published scarcity indicator and its 0.12 band are unchanged. The ratio is a step series (it changes only when a weekly release lands), so a value repeats until the next release moves the ratio or the level.
satiation_distance_columns.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.4.1, H.8), as read through the registry

release_lag.note: Declared 12 October 2026 (#598). The value on the row of day t uses only reads the as-of rule allows at 16:00 ET on t (availability_provenance), so the 16:00 ET decision of t reads it.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #630. The same release as nyfed_fr2004 (the New York Fed's Primary Dealer Statistics export, https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/pd/get/all/timeseries.csv, fetched 12 October 2026 with the repository's own fetch code), whose declaration this entry copies: see that entry's availability_provenance. The export keeps no vintages, so a later restatement cannot be seen; the six-business-day lag is the published schedule, not a measurement. The five series below run weekly from 2013-04-03 (the financing and fails series). Corrected by #680, which found the earlier statement of no gap wrong: the export withholds ('*') some weeks of three of them, 85 of 666 weekly dates for pd_repo_ust (2022 to 2025, longest run 12 weeks), 72 for pd_reverse_repo_ust (2022 to 2025, longest run 9 weeks) and 3 for pd_repo_mbs, and none for the two fails series; see docs/pivot/new-sources-withheld-weeks.md.
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed Primary Dealer Statistics release schedule: the figures for a Wednesday as-of date are published on the Thursday of the following week, six business days later; 16:30 ET is the conservative instant taken within that day.

coverage: primary dealer financing of US Treasuries (excluding TIPS) by repurchase agreements and by reverse repurchase agreements
primary dealer financing of agency mortgage-backed securities by repurchase agreements
primary dealer fails to deliver and to receive US Treasuries (cumulative over the week)
nyfed_pd_financing.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#630), and declared here and not in metadata/sources.json, which the final-test pre-registration freezes by its bytes. Values are USD millions in the export and USD billions in the columns. A value of '*' is a figure withheld for confidentiality: it is skipped and listed by parse_pd_suppressed, and a column is carried across the gap for at most data.WEEKLY_CARRY_MAX_STALENESS_DAYS (13 days) after the value's own as-of date, beyond which the cell is empty (#680; docs/decisions/weekly-carry.md). The tracked extract (tests/fixtures/snapshots/new_sources/nyfed_pd_financing/) holds only these five series up to 2025-12-31, with the digest and size of the 27 MB export beside it. Fails are cumulative over the week to the as-of date. The series are the 'total' lines (UTSETTOT: Treasuries excluding TIPS; FGMTOT: agency MBS other than ... as the export defines them); the export's own names are the only definition used.
nyfed_pd_financing.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Copied from nyfed_fr2004.release_lag (#630): the financing and fails series are in the same weekly export as the positions that entry reads, published together. The lag rests on the New York Fed's published Primary Dealer Statistics release schedule and not on the snapshot, which cannot corroborate it: the tracked fixture's manifest records the url it was downloaded from, https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/pd/get/all/timeseries.csv, and the retrieved_at of that download, 2026-09-14T00:31:00.991705+00:00, but one download shows only that the latest as-of date it carries, 2026-09-02, had been published by then -- a bound on the lag and not a measurement of it. Six business days from a Wednesday as-of date is the Thursday of the following week -- 2026-08-26 becomes available 2026-09-03 -- which is the calendar-week-plus-a-day gap the documented schedule describes. The directive that queued this adapter asked for 'calendar days 8' and a worst case of 9, and neither is expressible: src/repo_model/contract.py pins UNIT_FOR_BASIS['ref_date'] to 'business_days', so a calendar_days count on this basis is refused outright, and validate_release_lag requires worst_case_calendar_days to be at least days + 5, which puts the smallest admissible bound at 11 rather than 9. Six business days and eight calendar days name the same Thursday on a week with no holiday, and the business-day form is the one that shifts to Friday when one intervenes, which is what the directive's '(Thursday-holiday shift)' worst case describes. contract.py is human-owned, so both refusals are recorded here rather than worked around; 11 is conservative against 9 in the direction splits.py establishes as safe. Business days are counted on metadata/market_holidays.json, as for every other business-day source (#201), and the widest span on that table is 2018-12-21 to 2019-01-02, 12 calendar days, which is why worst_case_calendar_days is 12 and not 11 (#361, from #350).

nyfed_pd_financing.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the FR 2004 reporting instructions; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #630, from the tracked snapshot tests/fixtures/snapshots/treasury_auctions/auctions_2018_present.json (Fiscal Data auctions_query). Every auction in it with a result closes its competitive bidding at 14:30 ET or earlier (closing_time_comp: 11:30 AM for most bills, 01:00 PM for notes and bonds, 02:30 PM for two bills, and earlier times for a few), and the Treasury announces the results at the close, within minutes. The table serves the current rows and keeps no vintages, and a result is not restated. 15:00 ET on the auction date is declared, thirty minutes after the latest close, so the 16:00 decision of the auction day reads it; new_sources.require_result_public refuses a close later than 14:30.
availability_provenance.publication: Treasury auction results: announced at the close of competitive bidding on the auction date (closing_time_comp), served in Fiscal Data's auctions_query.

coverage: accepted amount, primary dealer and indirect bidder accepted amounts, total tendered, and the Fed rollover (SOMA) accepted and tendered, per auction, summed over the auctions of an auction date (SOMA added by #690: the shares and the cover leave it out)
treasury_auction_results.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#630). A column has a value only on a day with an auction that has a result, and is empty on every other day. Amounts are US dollars in the table and USD billions (accepted) or shares and a ratio (the others) in the columns. The table's record_date is the settlement date; the columns are dated by auction_date.
treasury_auction_results.provider: US Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service

release_lag.note: Declared 12 October 2026 (#630). The results of an auction on date d are declared public at 15:00 New York time on d, so the 16:00 decision of d reads it (availability_provenance).

treasury_auction_results.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the auction results schema; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #630. The same record as nyfed_on_rrp (the Desk's operation results, tests/fixtures/snapshots/on_rrp_inputs/nyfed_on_rrp), whose conservative declaration (16:00 ET on the next business day) this entry copies. participatingCpty is the number of counterparties that bid. A record the Desk wrote on a later day than its operation (lastUpdated after operationDate) is not read, because nothing shows which fields it changed; the Desk's counterparty-type split (propositions) is not read at all, because the Desk adds it a month later (tests/test_registry.py, A45).
availability_provenance.publication: New York Fed reverse repo operation results: the operation closes at 13:15 ET and the Desk's API carries the summary of results; 16:00 ET on the next business day is the conservative instant declared for the held amount accepted.

coverage: number of participating counterparties of the regular overnight reverse repo operation, per operation date
nyfed_on_rrp_counterparties.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#630). The largest participatingCpty among the regular Reverse Repo operations of an operationDate; repo operations and small-value exercises are left out; a date whose record was rewritten later is empty. The panel carries no value on a date without an operation.
nyfed_on_rrp_counterparties.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

release_lag.note: Copied from nyfed_on_rrp.release_lag (#630): the count of counterparties is a field of the same record as the amount accepted. Conservative, under docs/decisions/information-set.md (#45, step 3): a result is declared available at 16:00 ET on the next business day, not at its 13:15 close, because the Desk states no publication time. No value has been amended since publication: A45 compared 35 ALFRED vintages of RRPONTSYD against today's totalAmtAccepted on every single-operation day, and none differed. A record touched later (lastUpdated after the operation date) changed a note or the propositions, which are not read.

nyfed_on_rrp_counterparties.reviewed_note: Structural-zero semantics have not been reviewed against the operation-results schema; the empty declaration is not a finding.

availability_provenance.note: Recorded 12 October 2026 for #630. The same statement as treasury_dts_tga, whose declaration this entry copies: see that entry's availability_provenance. The statement for a business day is published at 4:00 PM ET on the next business day, and 16:30 ET is declared. The API keeps no vintages. The two lines are Table II's 'Public Debt Cash Issues' and 'Public Debt Cash Redemp.' (USD millions in the table), spelled '(Table III-B)' up to 2022 and '(Table IIIB)' after it in the saved responses; the reader treats the two spellings as one series. The tracked snapshots (tests/fixtures/snapshots/new_sources/treasury_dts_debt_cash/) were fetched on 12 October 2026, one request per line name and year, 2018 to 2025.
availability_provenance.publication: Daily Treasury Statement (Bureau of the Fiscal Service), Table II, Deposits and Withdrawals of Operating Cash, served as Fiscal Data's accounting/dts/deposits_withdrawals_operating_cash; published at 4:00 PM ET on the business day after the date it describes.

coverage: cash issues of public debt (deposits) and cash redemptions of public debt (withdrawals), daily, 2018 onwards in the tracked snapshots
treasury_dts_debt_cash.limitation: Off in every published declaration (#630). The fields are the two lines as new_sources.parse_dts_debt_cash names them (USD billions). dts_debt_net_bn is issues less redemptions on a day with both lines.
